title: Components, JSX & props
canDo: build components and pass data with props

blocks.md: Every React app is a tree of **components** — the only building block you need to learn once to build anything. A button, a nav bar, an entire page: all the same idea. This session you'll stop reading about components and start *seeing* them clearly, then go build them yourself in the best React course available.

blocks.canDo: build components and pass data with props
blocks.md: By the end of this session you will be able to **write a React component** (a function that returns JSX), follow JSX's syntax rules, and **pass data into a component with props** — understanding that props flow one way and are read-only inside the component.

**Components** are plain JavaScript functions whose name starts with a capital letter and whose return value is JSX — a syntax that looks like HTML but lives inside JS.

Three rules cover 90 % of JSX:
1. **One root element** — wrap siblings in a `<div>` or an empty `<>` fragment.
2. **Expressions in `{}`** — any JS expression goes inside curly braces; statements do not.
3. **`className` not `class`** — HTML attributes use camelCase (`onClick`, `htmlFor`, `className`).

**Props** are the arguments you pass *into* a component from its parent: `<Card title="Hi" />`. Inside the component they arrive as a single object (`function Card({ title }) {…}`). Props are **read-only** — a component never mutates its own props. Data always flows **down** the tree (parent → child).

### Primary resource — react.dev

Work through the **"Describing the UI"** chapter. It covers: your first component, importing/exporting, JSX rules, passing props, and conditional/list rendering. Each page has interactive sandboxes — do the challenges.

**Estimated time:** 60–70 min · Come back when you finish the chapter.

blocks.md: **JSX is compiled, not magic.** Under the hood `<Card title="Hi" />` becomes `React.createElement(Card, { title: 'Hi' })`. You never need to call that function directly, but knowing it exists makes the "one root element" and "expressions only" rules make complete sense.

questions.question: What must a React component return?
options: An HTML DOM element created with document.createElement
questions.explanation: A component is a function that returns JSX — React's syntax for describing UI — or null when it renders nothing.

questions.question: Which statement about props is correct?
options: Props flow from parent to child and are read-only inside the receiving component
A component can mutate its props to update the parent
Props flow from child to parent so children can control their parents
Props are only available in class components
questions.explanation: Data always flows down the component tree. A component reads its props but never changes them — that one-way constraint keeps React apps predictable.

questions.question: Which of the following is valid JSX?
questions.explanation: JSX uses className (not class), allows any JS *expression* inside {}, and requires a single root element. Statements like if blocks are not expressions and cannot go directly in {}.

blocks.md:
### What you covered

- A **component** is a JS function (capital name) that returns JSX.
- JSX rules: **one root**, `{expressions}`, **`className`** for CSS classes.
- **Props** pass data *into* a component from the outside; they are always **read-only** inside.
bullets: JSX: one root element, {} for expressions, className not class
Props flow parent → child and are read-only
